newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich urges more women Republican candidates.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich urges more women Republican candidates.

text.p: Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Friday he hoped half of his party's candidates would be women by the year 2000.

"Nothing is better for this party than to have half of our candidates female as early as possible in 1998 and 2000 -- as soon as we can get it," Gingrich said in a speech to the National Federation of Republican Women.
"Not because we're looking for quota, but because the objective fact is, if 53 percent of the population is female, then we ought to be reaching out to the total talent pool that's available.

"So my challenge to you is find the right candidate, help them win a primary and then help them win an election. Nothing will do more to help us reach out to women in American than to simply have good effective, articulate women speaking for the party," he said.
"And if you can't find anybody else, if you're an American citizen legally of age and not a convicted felon, you run."

Fifty-two women were among the 435 members of the House of Representatives elected last November -- 36 of them Democrats and 16 Republicans. The 100-member Senate has nine women -- six Democrats and three Republicans.
The two major parties nominated 115 women candidates for House seats last year and nine women in 35 Senate races.
President Clinton, a Democrat, won a strong majority of votes from women in his successful reelection bid against Republican Bob Dole last November.
Gingrich said Republicans under his leadership were the first party to have three women in House leadership positions and the first to name a woman as clerk of the House.

He also promised that a large statue of women's sufferage leaders Susan B. Anthony, Lucretia Mott and Elizabth Cady Stanton would be moved from the first floor of the Capitol to a more prominent place in the second floor Rotunda.

The statue was placed in the Capitol in 1922 soon after women were granted the right to vote in the United States. It is so large a crane will be needed to lift it to the Rotunda near statues of other national leaders such as George Washington and Abraham Lincoln.
"This Congress, under the Republicans, with (Senate Majority Leader) Trent Lott and I at the ceremony, we will move the statue to the Rotunda," Gingrich said.
